correctness.rationale: The chord-angle half-angle geometry yields independent uniform phase and triangular angular difference; the transformed dot product has a direct trigonometric sign characterization. Its exact conditional integral reduces by symmetry, integration by parts, a sine substitution and a central-binomial series to the claimed dilogarithm law. Nondegeneracy and at most one obtuse angle handle counting; correct endpoints, monotonicity and asymptotics follow analytically. Direct Cartesian Monte Carlo (220000 triples) and independent quadrature agree with the derived formula. Finite tests alone are not proof.

value.rationale: The affine deformation of iid uniform-circle vertices is a canonical random boundary triangle model. Acute-angle status is not affine-invariant, so the complete shape law is a natural geometric probability invariant; strict circular optimality, sharp quadratic rigidity, thin-ellipse logarithmic rarity, and the nontrivial comparison to off-center circle containment give it mathematical substance beyond a substitution or elementary normalization.
